questions.question: What is the main use case for Building RAG Systems?
options: Traditional software development
AI-powered content generation and processing
Database management
Network security
questions.explanation: Building RAG Systems is primarily used for AI-powered content generation and intelligent processing tasks.

questions.question: What is the core trust invariant of a RAG answer?
options: Its factual claims must be supported by authorized, attributable evidence.
Its language must sound confident and complete.
Its vector similarity score must exceed a universal threshold.
It must always include the maximum possible number of chunks.
questions.explanation: Fluency and similarity do not establish grounding. Support, authorization, and attribution must hold for the evidence behind each claim.

questions.question: When should a team add an advanced retrieval stage?
options: Whenever a larger model is available.
After a sliced evaluation identifies a repeatable retrieval failure the stage can address.
Before building a single-query baseline.
Whenever the context window is longer than the source document.
questions.explanation: Every extra stage adds work and failure modes. Add it for a named, measured gap such as missing multi-part evidence or vocabulary mismatch.

questions.question: What is the core trust invariant of a production knowledge graph?
options: Every node must have a human-readable name.
Every accepted node and edge remains traceable to evidence, policy, and time.
Every query must traverse at least three hops.
The language model decides which extracted facts are true.
questions.explanation: Traceable provenance and policy let operators verify, retract, authorize, and reproduce graph claims. A readable label or model confidence is not enough.

questions.question: What is the core production invariant of a RAG answer?
options: Every factual claim can be traced to authorized, versioned evidence or the system abstains
The generator always receives the maximum context window
Dense retrieval always returns more documents than sparse retrieval
The model answers from parametric memory whenever retrieval is slow
questions.explanation: RAG is trustworthy only when evidence identity, authorization, freshness, and claim support survive through the answer. Missing support should trigger containment, not invention.

questions.question: What is the core grounding invariant for a RAG answer?
options: No evidence, no grounded claim.
Every query must use agentic retrieval.
A large context window guarantees correctness.
A model confidence score replaces source citations.
questions.explanation: The answer service should make material claims only when selected, authorized evidence supports them; otherwise it should refuse or state what is missing.

questions.question: Why should an ANN index be evaluated against exact nearest-neighbor results on representative queries?
options: Exact results provide the ground truth needed to measure recall@k
Exact search always has lower latency than ANN search
ANN indexes cannot return similarity scores
Exact search automatically enforces tenant authorization
questions.explanation: Recall@k asks how many exact top-k neighbors the approximate search recovered. Without an exact reference set, the team cannot quantify approximation loss.
